text: GROD reduces FPR@95 on image OOD detection from 21.97% (baseline) to 0.12%, an improvement of over 21 percentage points (Table 1).
GROD improves AUROC on image classification OOD tasks from 93.62% to 99.98% (Table 1).
On text classification OOD tasks using BERT, GROD improves FPR@95 by 12.89 percentage points and AUROC by 2.27 percentage points over baselines (Table 3).

Theorem 1 (Informal Theorem 4) establishes that OOD detection learnability for transformers requires finite training data and an OOD misclassification penalty that exceeds the ID misclassification penalty (Section 3, Theorem 1).
Ablation studies show the binary loss term, synthetic OOD generation module, and Mahalanobis distance filtering each individually contribute to GROD's overall performance gains (Table 4).
GROD outperforms baseline OOD detectors MSP, ODIN, VIM, GEN, ASH, G-ODIN, NPOS, and CIDER on CIFAR-10-based image OOD benchmarks (Table 1).
